title: Speech, stone tool-making and the two-step evolution of language
author: Dana M Cataldo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jyycpxw
materials: Dana Michelle Cataldo, Andrea Bamberg Migliano, Lucio Vinicius

steps.title: Participant Onboarding and Consent
steps.instruction: Welcome the participant and obtain informed consent.

substeps.instruction: Present the consent form to the participant for reading and signing.
Ask the participant if they have any questions about the study.

steps.title: Equipment Provision
steps.instruction: Provide the participant with necessary safety gear and materials.

substeps.instruction: Distribute goggles, gloves, a protective coat, and a breathing mask.
Provide a selection of flint and hammerstones.

steps.title: Introductory Phase
steps.instruction: Introduce the experiment's aim and provide a basic demonstration of tool utility.

substeps.instruction: Explain that the aim is to understand how language contributed to the evolution of stone tool technologies and cumulative culture in hominin language.
Provide an information sheet on flint tools and their use.
Allow the participant to try a flake on a stick to understand what makes a useful flake.
After 5 minutes, conclude the phase and retrieve the information sheet, flake, and stick.

steps.title: Teaching Phase
steps.instruction: Instruct the participant based on their assigned group (Full Language/Gesture/Speech or Control).

substeps.instruction: For Full Language, Gesture, and Speech groups: Explain how to make flakes and assist the participant using the assigned communication method.
For Control group: Place demonstration cores and flakes in front of the participant for examination without providing any instruction.
After 5 minutes, conclude the phase and inform the participant that no further instruction will be provided.

steps.title: Testing Phase
steps.instruction: Allow the participant to produce viable flakes independently.

substeps.instruction: Instruct the participant to choose a flint core from the pile and a hammerstone from the selection.
Instruct the participant to make as many viable flakes as possible.
Stop the session after 20 minutes or when the participant indicates they are finished.

steps.title: Classifying Phase
steps.instruction: Have the participant categorize the produced flakes.

substeps.instruction: Instruct the participant to classify flakes as viable or non-viable and place them into two separate piles.

steps.title: Post-Test Questionnaire
steps.instruction: Collect subjective data on the instruction received.

substeps.instruction: Present the Post-Test Questionnaire asking the participant to rank agreement with three statements on a scale from 1 to 5.

steps.title: Sample Collection and Wrap-up
steps.instruction: Collect all materials and finalize the session.

substeps.instruction: Collect all flakes and cores produced by the participant.
Place samples in a plastic bag and register the participant ID and condition.
